A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 19-page versions of the same research work. Their text, figures, tables, equations and appendices support reliable comparison despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, retrieval experiments, error analyses and human assessments of interpretations in Sections 4–5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and reports revised human evaluation of generated interpretations, including inter-annotator agreement.

M1.justification: The retrieval, atomic-assumption generation, validation and any-false-assumption adjudication procedures remain unchanged. Added notation and revised model documentation do not establish a new algorithm or component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate on (QA)2, CREPE and FalseQA and use BoolQ and FEVER in supervised transfer experiments. Newly discussed benchmarks in related work are not evaluated.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain MiniCheck, RoBERTa, direct and generated-evidence prompting, OpenAI o1, and the same LLM configurations. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Generated-interpretation assessment changes from one graduate annotator in v1 Appendix D.1 to two in v2 Appendix C.1. Appendix A.7 also replaces GPT-4 (0125-Preview) with GPT-4o (2024-08-07) for transformation and assumption generation; this revises the reported setting without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The error analysis gains an 'All Other' category and an additional example in v2 Table 5. Existing evidence-count sensitivity tests, smaller-model analyses and interpretation-error cases are retained.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix C.1 newly reports Cohen's kappa for generated-interpretation assessment: 0.65, 0.68 and 0.73 for (QA)2, CREPE and FalseQA. Existing McNemar tests and agreement statistics for atomic-assumption annotation remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Under the revised human-assessment protocol, Section 5 replaces GPT-4o accuracies 0.88/0.71/0.90 with 0.86/0.67/0.93 and Llama 3 70B accuracies 0.84/0.67/0.83 with 0.81/0.66/0.84, in dataset order (QA)2/CREPE/FalseQA. Table 5 adds residual error percentages of 50% FP and 35% FN. Main benchmark and appendix sensitivity scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 introduces task notation and expresses the existing adjudication rule as a conjunction. These formalize the already described binary task and aggregation procedure without adding substantive mathematical assumptions, reasoning, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about retrieval benefits, interpretable atomic assumptions, performance across three datasets and computational efficiency. Rewording does not materially change their scope.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same explanations concerning hallucinations, information lost through question-to-statement conversion and smaller-model limitations. The limitations concerning reproducibility, retrieval dependence, computational overhead and unmeasurable assumption recall are substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a code/data repository link where v1 promised release upon acceptance. It also revises model identifiers, clarifies generation-length settings and corrects prompt documentation, including Figure 7's final hard-coded 'Yes' becoming an output placeholder. Most retrieval details are relocated rather than newly disclosed.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion and citations for Peng et al. (2025), Zhao et al. (2024) and Yang et al. (2024), covering related unanswerability problems. The Vu et al. (2023) discussion/reference is removed. The central positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Widespread editing accompanies substantial narrative reorganization: dataset descriptions and retrieval procedures move into the main text, baseline subsections are consolidated, results receive separate baseline/retrieval/atomic-assumption subsections, and appendices are reorganized. Task notation and acknowledgments are also added.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn with consolidated inputs and correctness labels. The dataset table moves from the appendix to the main text, the error table gains a row, and table emphasis and float placement change. Most figures and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Two-annotator evaluation with reported agreement strengthens the interpretation assessment. The code/data access link, corrected prompts and clearer organization also improve documentation and readability. The gains are limited: central experimental evidence is largely unchanged, and the main text and appendix still differ on GPT-4 versus GPT-4o for question transformation.
